ip_top_stories.title: [Guest post] Getty Images v Stability AI: the parties' submissions and key points from the appeal
ip_top_stories.summary: IPKat publishes a guest post analysing the submissions and key arguments presented by both parties in the Getty Images v Stability AI appeal. The case is a major AI copyright litigation proceeding in the UK courts, with the BPI also filing a supporting brief backing Getty's position.

ip_top_stories.title: Court of Justice asked to clarify copyright rules for AI training and chatbot outputs
ip_top_stories.summary: A referral has been made to the Court of Justice of the EU seeking clarification on copyright rules as they apply to AI training data and the outputs generated by AI chatbots. The ruling could have significant implications for how AI companies operate under EU law.

ip_top_stories.title: Universal and Sony Want Suno's Newest AI Models Exposed in 60K-Recording Copyright Battle
ip_top_stories.summary: Universal Music and Sony are pushing for discovery of Suno's newest AI music generation models as part of an ongoing copyright lawsuit involving around 60,000 recordings. The labels are seeking to examine whether the latest models were also trained on copyrighted material without authorisation.

ip_top_stories.title: ByteDance sued by automotive photography firm EVOX, alleging TikTok parent copied 7,095 images to train its Seedream AI image generator
ip_top_stories.summary: Automotive photography company EVOX has filed a lawsuit against ByteDance, alleging the TikTok parent company copied 7,095 of its images to train its Seedream AI image generation model without authorisation. The case adds to growing litigation against AI companies over use of copyrighted visual material for training data.

ip_top_stories.title: Guest Post — Beyond the Download: What Counts as Scholarly Content Use in the Age of AI?
ip_top_stories.summary: A guest post on The Scholarly Kitchen examines how traditional definitions of content use in academic publishing are being challenged by AI, questioning whether training, retrieval-augmented generation, and AI-mediated access constitute new forms of use requiring new licensing frameworks. The piece argues the publishing industry needs updated metrics and agreements to reflect how scholarly content is now consumed.

ip_further_links.title: Getty v Stability AI appeal: BPI backs Getty in UK court
ip_further_links.summary: The BPI (British Phonographic Industry) has filed a supporting brief backing Getty Images in its UK copyright appeal against Stability AI.

ip_further_links.title: China's Supreme People's Court Issues Its First Comprehensive Guidance on AI-Related Disputes: An IP Enforcement Perspective
ip_further_links.summary: China's Supreme People's Court has issued its first comprehensive guidance on resolving AI-related IP disputes, with significant implications for how AI copyright and enforcement matters will be handled in Chinese courts.

ip_further_links.title: Publishers Push to Keep Search Access While Setting AI Terms
ip_further_links.summary: Publishers are seeking to negotiate AI licensing terms that preserve access to search while establishing controls over how their content is used to train AI systems.

ip_further_links.title: Paul Kelly pleads for Albanese to 'show some backbone' over AI as creatives campaign for copyright protections
ip_further_links.summary: Australian musician Paul Kelly has joined a campaign by the creative sector urging the Albanese government to strengthen copyright protections against unauthorised AI use of creative works.

ip_further_links.title: 'Deeply flawed': Former ACCC boss slams opt-out AI copyright plan
ip_further_links.summary: Australia's former competition regulator chief has criticised the government's proposed opt-out AI copyright framework as deeply flawed, adding to pressure for stronger protections for creators.

ip_further_links.title: Magabala Books urges reform over Indigenous stories used to train AI without permission
ip_further_links.summary: Australian Indigenous publisher Magabala Books has called for legislative reform after Indigenous stories were used without consent to train AI systems, raising concerns about cultural rights and copyright.

ip_further_links.title: Australian creative sector launches campaign against unauthorised AI use of copyright material
ip_further_links.summary: Australia's creative industries have launched a coordinated public campaign demanding stronger legal protections against AI companies using copyright material without authorisation or compensation.

ip_further_links.title: AI in the patent industry: Have you read the terms and conditions?
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat examines the terms and conditions of AI tools being used in the patent industry, raising questions about IP ownership and confidentiality risks for legal professionals.

ip_further_links.title: Tamil Nadu Publisher Held for Selling 5,316 AI-Titled Books to State Libraries
ip_further_links.summary: A Tamil Nadu publisher has been arrested for allegedly selling over 5,000 AI-generated books to state libraries, raising concerns about quality, authenticity, and the misuse of AI in book publishing.

ip_further_links.title: Madbouly opens WIPO copyright conference in New Capital as AI tests protection for creators
ip_further_links.summary: Egypt's Prime Minister opened a WIPO copyright conference examining how AI is challenging existing creator protections, with international policymakers gathering to discuss frameworks for the AI era.
